paragraphs.text: What is headless Shopify? In a standard Shopify store, a Liquid theme controls how the storefront looks. In a headless setup, that theme is replaced by a custom storefront, built with a modern framework, which reads products, collections and carts from Shopify through the Shopify Storefront API. Shopify still runs the admin, inventory, payments and checkout.

The result is a custom Shopify storefront with complete design freedom, faster pages and the ability to combine products with rich content from other systems, while your team keeps managing the store in the Shopify admin they already know.

Headless vs Liquid themes comes down to flexibility against simplicity. Liquid themes are quicker and cheaper to launch, work with most Shopify apps out of the box and are easy to edit. Headless storefronts offer full design control, faster performance and richer content, but they cost more to build and some apps that change the storefront need custom integration.

When should a Shopify store go headless? Usually when the brand has outgrown theme limits: it needs a distinctive shopping experience, very fast mobile pages, content-heavy product storytelling, or one storefront serving several markets and channels. For most new or small stores, a well-built theme is the better first step, and we will say so honestly.

sections.h2: What Headless Shopify Services Does Teknoppy Offer?

items.title: Shopify Hydrogen Development
items.text: Shopify Hydrogen development uses Hydrogen, Shopify's own React-based framework built specifically for headless storefronts. It includes ready-made commerce components for products, carts and customer accounts, which speeds up development. Analytics, product search and personalisation are added through Shopify-compatible services rather than theme apps.

items.title: Shopify Oxygen Hosting
items.text: Shopify Oxygen hosting is Shopify's global hosting service for Hydrogen storefronts. Pages are served close to shoppers, deployments are managed from your Shopify account, and there is no separate server to maintain.

items.title: Headless Shopify With Next JS
items.html:
Headless Shopify with Next JS suits brands that also run content-heavy sections, blogs or other web apps on Next.js, or that prefer hosting outside Shopify. It connects to the same Storefront API.

Hydrogen vs Next JS commerce: Hydrogen is the closest fit to Shopify, with built-in commerce tools and Oxygen hosting. Next.js offers a larger general ecosystem and more hosting choices. We recommend one during discovery based on your team, content needs and hosting preferences.

items.title: Content Alongside Products
items.html: Many brands want long-form guides, recipes, lookbooks or ingredient stories next to their products. We connect a headless CMS or Shopify's own content tools to the storefront, so your marketing team can publish rich pages without touching code, and every story can link directly to the products it features.

items.title: Shopify Plus Headless
items.text: Shopify Plus headless projects suit high-volume brands that need several storefronts, advanced checkout customisation, B2B features or many markets from one organisation. We plan the headless architecture around your Plus features.

sections.h2: Headless Shopify Projects We Commonly Build

paragraphs.text: Typical headless Shopify development projects include fashion and beauty storefronts with rich lookbooks, wellness and Ayurveda brands that pair products with detailed guides, food and spice brands selling to India and the Gulf, and lifestyle brands that run several regional stores from one Shopify organisation.

Shopify Markets and localization let one headless storefront sell in several countries, with local currencies, languages, prices and domains. Headless Shopify for GCC brands can show Arabic and English storefronts with right-to-left layouts, Gulf currencies and regional shipping rules, all managed from one Shopify admin. Each market can also show its own offers and featured collections.

items.title: A Headless Shopify Readiness Audit First
items.text: Before any build, a headless Shopify readiness audit reviews your current store, apps, content, traffic, conversion data and budget. You receive a written answer on whether going headless will pay off, which apps need alternatives, and what the project will involve.

items.title: Proof and Accountability
items.text: Vivek Menon, CTO of Evosyz in Kochi, says Teknoppy "created an appealing website that represents our brand perfectly." Founder Sanal Edison reviews the architecture and search plan of every project before development begins.

paragraphs.text: Is headless Shopify worth it? For established brands with strong traffic, it often is. Faster pages, a distinctive experience and richer product content can lift conversion and average order value. For smaller stores, the extra build and maintenance cost may outweigh the gains, and a theme-based store is usually wiser.
Our readiness audit puts numbers on this decision, so you invest only when the case is clear.

sections.h2: How Much Does Headless Shopify Cost?

paragraphs.text: How much does headless Shopify cost? It depends on the number of page templates, markets, languages, integrations and custom features. Headless builds cost more than theme-based stores, and you should also budget for ongoing development, because new storefront features are built in code rather than added through theme settings.
Every project is quoted after the readiness audit. Each quote for headless Shopify development is fixed for the agreed scope and lists exactly what is included.

items.q: Does checkout change in a headless store?
items.a: Shoppers still complete payment through Shopify's secure checkout, so payment methods, taxes and order handling stay the same. The custom storefront hands the cart to Shopify at the checkout step.

items.q: How long does headless Shopify development take?
items.a: A single-market D2C storefront usually takes 8 to 12 weeks of headless Shopify development. Multi-market or Shopify Plus projects take 12 to 16 weeks. We confirm the timeline in writing after the readiness audit.

items.q: Can my team still manage products in Shopify?
items.a: Yes. Products, prices, inventory, discounts and orders are all managed in the Shopify admin exactly as before. Only the storefront that customers see is new.
